title: Add lightweight RAG local debug prober with indexed mocks and HTTP adapter
author: Aisha Moreno
description: Summary: Adds a compact RAG local debug prober quickstart intended for developer onboarding and iterative debugging. The quickstart bundles: 1) an HTTP adapter shim to emulate external tool calls; 2) an indexed-mock store for reproducible retrieval fixtures; 3) a lightweight prober CLI that can run trapped scenarios (offline) and produce traceable session artifacts; and 4) telemetry probe hooks for step-level timing and token accounting. Motivation: teams repeatedly requested a small reproducible devkit that mirrors production retrieval+tool-calling behavior but runs without remote infra. This quickstart targets contributor friction: zero cloud credentials to run, snapshotable mock indexes, and easy toggles for streaming vs non-streaming flows. Changeset overview: added quickstart scaffold under quickstarts/rag-local-prober, new prober CLI (node/ts), an HTTP adapter written in minimal express-style shim, two example retrieval index snapshots (small, 1k docs and tiny 10-doc), structured output validators, and a tracing exporter that writes compact JSON session traces for local replay. The description below is a continuous narrative (no separate files): Context and design: keep the runtime close to what Redwood serving expects (session tokens, step boundaries, tool-call hooks) while decoupling from the service control plane. The HTTP adapter accepts the same POST /call tool shape used in our agent samples and returns configurable canned responses or artifact echoes; it is purposefully minimal to be usable with Playwright or unit tests. The indexed-mock store implements a tiny on-disk inverted index with near-constant startup cost and supports incremental delta loading so developers can swap in new snapshots without rebuilding binaries. CLI and dev loop: prober run --scenario=browser-search --index=small creates a reproducible run, emits step traces to /tmp/rag-prober/traces, and prints a compact summary with token counts and latency percentiles. Integration with local authoring: the quickstart includes a devcontainer and npm scripts for one-command start (dev: up). The quickstart is intentionally opinionated about defaults (low-latency, small batch sizes, streaming off) but exposes configuration flags for batching, prefix-caching, and tool timeouts. Security and credentialing: the prober includes an optional credential injection step that accepts a local API token file; by default it runs in a credentialless mode and warns when tokens are present to avoid accidental leakage. Release rationale: this is developer tooling only (not for production) and reduces authoring iteration time for retrieval-and-tool workflows.
commits_summary: 4 commits: 1) scaffold quickstart and README; 2) add prober CLI, HTTP adapter and index loader; 3) add example snapshots and structured-output lints; 4) test matrix and CI job updates (node 18/20). Each commit contains small, focused changes with unit tests for adapter and index loader.
